draft.title: Hypothetical Context Length Increase Causes Major Slowdown on 16GB GPU: What's Next?
draft.body: I'm investigating a hypothetical performance issue in a local LLM setup. The system is equipped with a 16 GB GPU [F1]. We observed a drastic slowdown when increasing the context length from 2048 to 8192 tokens. This is purely a hypothetical scenario at this stage; specific model and runtime versions haven't been logged yet [F3], and there's no current data pointing to driver, system RAM, or model file corruption as causes [F4]. My primary question is: what are the most probable technical bottlenecks that could manifest as such a severe latency jump when scaling context size on a constrained 16GB VRAM setup? Could this be related to how the attention mechanism scales with input length, or perhaps inefficiencies in managing the KV cache given the VRAM limitations? Any insights into where to focus hypothetical debugging efforts would be greatly appreciated.
